summary: Backend-only regression + new-feature testing for the RDP Worker fleet. Added /app/backend/tests/test_workers.py (16 tests) covering worker CRUD, worker Bearer auth, heartbeat, atomic claim with capacity & name-resolution semantics, progress, complete, and the new poller grace window. Ran the full backend suite (iteration_1 + new): 42 passed, 1 pre-existing skip, 0 failed in 97.75s against the public preview URL.

minor.issue: Claim loop issues N sequential find_one_and_update round-trips and a separate _resolve_names() Mongo lookup per task. Functionally correct, but for a worker pulling max_tasks=50 against a custom name-file, that is 50+ round-trips per claim call. Consider a single bulk find_and_update + memoising name resolution per name_source within one request.

Grace branch uses `worker_id: {"$nin": [None]}` which matches worker-owned tasks correctly, but after the 60s grace it marks them `status=completed` (not `failed`). The accompanying code comment says 'mark failed (worker silent)'. Behaviour is consistent and tested, but the status disagrees with the comment / intent — silent-worker tasks may want status='failed' with an `error` populated so the UI can distinguish from a happy completion.

action_items: (Optional) Resolve the poller comment-vs-behaviour mismatch: either change the grace-out branch to `status=failed` + `error='worker timed out'`, or update the comment to match the current 'completed' semantics.
(Optional perf) Batch claim to reduce per-task Mongo round-trips when max_tasks is large.
(Optional usage accounting) Cancelled/failed tasks still hold their members against `users.usage`. If that's intentional, document it; otherwise, decrement usage on cancel/fail.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:828-836 — grace branch marks `completed` despite the comment saying 'failed'. Pick one; UI will look at task.status to render error rows.

server.py:587 — `range(min(max_tasks, capacity_left))` is correct but the loop body's find_one_and_update doesn't bump `current_load` on the worker. So if a worker calls /claim repeatedly between heartbeats, `capacity_left` doesn't shrink until the next heartbeat reports the new load. Consider `$inc: current_load` atomically in the same call, or rely on heartbeats coming faster than claim cadence.
server.py:582 — capacity_left snapshot is read once before the loop; race if worker heartbeats during a long claim. Minor.
server.py:826 — `'$or': [{'worker_id': None}, {'worker_id': {'$exists': False}}]` is repeated in 3 places. Extract a helper / constant.

Token format is fine, but the secret is bcrypt-hashed (~80ms per verify). On a busy poll/claim loop a worker will trigger one bcrypt verify per request. Worth knowing — consider HMAC(SHA256, server_secret) for the worker channel if QPS climbs.
Good: worker token_hash is excluded from /api/workers list via projection (verified).
Good: all worker-auth failures return string `detail`, not a Pydantic validation array (verified).
